REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION
THURSDAY - JULY 18, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.gov and at the City Manager’s Office, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 3rd floor, Cerritos, CA, 90703 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the Commission after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection at the City Manager’s Office during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1311 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The Commission, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 5.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the City Manager's Office no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the Commission prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Manager's Office at (562) 916-1311 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION HELD
  July 18, 2024

Regular Fine Arts and Historical Commission Meeting
July 18, 2024
City Council Chambers
Bloomfield Avenue at 183rd Street
Cerritos, California 90703

PRESENT:  Commissioner Matthew S. Kauble
  Vice Chair Kelly Colwell
  Chair C.J. Villaluna

ABSENT:  Commissioner Michelle Guerrero
  Commissioner Parimal Shah

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villaluna called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Cerritos City Council
  Chamber, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, California.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Villaluna.

3.  ROLL CALL

  All Members of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission were present, except
  Commissioners Guerrero and Shah.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to excuse the absences of Commissioners
  Guerrero and Shah. Vice Chair Colwell seconded the motion, which carried with
  Commissioners Guerrero and Shah, absent.

4.  PRESENTATIONS

4A.  Presentation to former Chair of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission

  Assistant City Manager Kathleen Jung Matsumoto reported this item will be continued
  to the following Fine Arts and Historical Commission meeting as the former Chair is
  absent at this time.

5.  PUBLIC COMMENTS AND SUGGESTIONS

  Chair Villaluna invited public comments.

  There were no public comments and Chair Villaluna closed this portion of the
  meeting.

6.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
 6A.  Thursday, May 16, 2024, 7:00 p.m., Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  Regular meeting minutes.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to approve the minutes of the regular
  meeting of May 16, 2024, 7:00 p.m., as presented. Vice Chair Colwell seconded the
  motion, which carried, 3-0, by roll call vote with Commissioners Guerrero and Shah,
  absent.

7.  NEW AND OLD BUSINESS

7A.  Review and Consideration of a Program to Exhibit Maquettes from the City
  of Cerritos Public Art Collection in the Cerritos Library

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented details of the staff report.

  There were no public comments on this item.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble to approve the program to exhibit Maquettes from
  the City of Cerritos Public Art Collection in the Cerritos Library, as presented in the
  staff report. Vice Chair Colwell seconded the motion, which carried, 3-0, by roll call
  vote with Commissioners Guerrero and Shah, absent.

8.  COMMUNICATIONS

8A.  Reports from Commission Staff Liaison

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented an update of current public art projects
  including the Public Safety Memorial; reported that the “Milking Time” historical
  artwork featuring a cow, farmer, children and dog was approved by City Council with
  changes that were communicated to the artist and listed those changes. She added
  that staff is working on the contract which will be presented to City Council at its
  meeting on July 25, 2024 and addressed changes that have been made to the City
  website.

  Director of Community and Cultural Services Annie Hylton provided an update on the
  status of the City’s website and noted it is in the last phase of the project.

8B.  Reports from Fine Arts and Historical Commission Members

  Commissioner Kauble talked about the book “The Economic Power of Public Art;”
  suggested the possibility of holding an annual Community Art Festival on the Civic
  Center grounds or Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts and discussed starting
  small and building it up. Additionally, he spoke about the possibility of working with
  the Cerritos Auto Square and Hasbro to develop a line of Autobot statues that could
  be displayed at the Cerritos Auto Square and sold as toys at dealerships to attract
  tourists to the west side of the City and asked about asking City Council to allow the
  Fine Arts and Historical Commission to study the matter.

  Subsequent to discussion, the Commission concurred to direct staff to place both
  items on the upcoming agenda for discussion.
